_ghi_chu_en: EN-ALL GĐ 4 (agent C) — bản phủ tiếng Anh cho "Two charts together": 120 câu khác nhau (5 tiêu chí × 3 mức × 8 quan hệ), không doạ, không phán chia tay, không vật phẩm. Ban biên tập viết lại, chờ người bản xứ duyệt.

menh.mo_ta: Your basic temperament and how you react when happy or tired.

can.mo_ta: Whether the two of you easily agree when a choice has to be made.

chi.mo_ta: Daily habits, and how comfortable it feels to be around each other.

cung_phi.mo_ta: Taste in where to live and work, and how to arrange a space.

tu_vi.ten: Where the Zi Wei charts meet
tu_vi.mo_ta: Which areas of your life the other person's birth year lands in.

menh.hop: Your natures give each other energy
menh.binh_hoa: Similar natures, easy to read each other
menh.can_dung_hoa: Different rhythms, so you need to give way

can.hop: You easily agree on how to do things
can.binh_hoa: Each has their own view, without getting in the way
can.can_dung_hoa: You may compete over which way to go

chi.hop: Matching zodiac animals, comfortable to be around
chi.binh_hoa: Neutral zodiac animals, it depends on how you treat each other
chi.can_dung_hoa: Zodiac animals that rub over small things

cung_phi.hop: Easy to choose a home or workplace together
cung_phi.can_dung_hoa: Different views on where to live and how to arrange it

tu_vi.hop: The other person brings ease right where this relationship lives
tu_vi.binh_hoa: The charts touch lightly; it is up to the two of you to grow it
tu_vi.can_dung_hoa: The core of this relationship easily fills up with expectations

nguoi_yeu.y: Your natures make up for each other: when one of you dips, the other can usually lift them back up.
nguoi_yeu.nen: When your partner is tired, ask whether they want to talk or to be left in peace, then do exactly that.

vo_chong.y: At home, the two of you split tasks by strengths without long discussions.
vo_chong.nen: Write down who is good at which household job and hand it over fully, so nobody has to remind anybody.

ban_be.y: Being together usually leaves you both feeling better, and good news doubles.
ban_be.nen: Keep a regular habit of meeting, such as coffee at the end of each month, so this good fit does not fade.

dong_nghiep.y: Working on the same task, you pick up where the other leaves off: one starts, the other finishes.
dong_nghiep.nen: Split work by stage — who opens it, who polishes it — and note it clearly on the task board.

doi_tac.y: Your strengths complement each other, so together you easily make a well-rounded business team.
doi_tac.nen: Put each side's contribution in writing, including the effort that is not measured in money.

sep.y: You and your manager click easily: what you do is often exactly what they need.
sep.nen: Send a short report each week so they can clearly see your contribution.

cha_me_con.y: Parent and child lift each other: one person's advice usually suits the other's character.
cha_me_con.nen: Spend one session a week doing something small together, like cooking a dish or going for a walk.

gia_dinh.y: Among the relatives, the two of you are often the pair who help each other when the family has something on.
gia_dinh.nen: Take on one family task together, such as organising an anniversary or a house repair, so this good fit gets put to use.

nguoi_yeu.y: You share the same basic nature, so you read each other easily but can also dig your heels in at the same time.
nguoi_yeu.nen: When you are both tense, agree that whoever says "pause" first gets ten quiet minutes from the other.

vo_chong.y: As a couple you are alike at heart, so housework causes little disagreement, but you may both overlook the same thing.
vo_chong.nen: Every quarter, go over the things you both tend to forget, like paperwork, insurance and repairs.

ban_be.y: You share the same taste and need little explaining, but you may both shy away from trying new things.
ban_be.nen: Now and then, plan something neither of you has ever done, so the friendship has new stories.

dong_nghiep.y: You work the same way, so coordination is smooth, but you may both miss the same angle.
dong_nghiep.nen: Before handing in shared work, ask a third person to read it over.

doi_tac.y: You run business the same way, so you agree easily but lack someone to argue the other side.
doi_tac.nen: Bring in an outside adviser or independent accountant to review big decisions.

sep.y: You and your manager think alike, so you rarely clash, but they may assume you already understand everything.
sep.nen: Ask about the finish criteria right when you take on a task; do not guess from your own view.

cha_me_con.y: Parent and child have similar characters: love comes easily, but so do the same kinds of anger.
cha_me_con.nen: When one of you gets heated, the other leaves the room for a while and comes back to continue.

gia_dinh.y: These relatives have similar natures and understand each other quickly, but old stories tend to be brought up again.
gia_dinh.nen: Agree not to bring up the past at family meals.

nguoi_yeu.y: Your basic rhythms differ: one wants speed, the other wants calm, and it is easy to misread each other when tired.
nguoi_yeu.nen: Say clearly "this is what I need right now" instead of waiting for the other to guess.

vo_chong.y: Under pressure you react differently, so money or children can easily turn into arguments.
vo_chong.nen: Set a fixed weekly time to discuss household matters, and do not settle big things outside it.

ban_be.y: Your rhythms differ, and at times one of you finds the other too much or too cautious.
ban_be.nen: Meet up for things you both enjoy, and invite each other less to things only one of you is keen on.

dong_nghiep.y: You work at different speeds: one acts at once, the other needs to think it through, and you can get impatient with each other.
dong_nghiep.nen: Agree deadlines for each part from the start so nobody has to chase anybody.

doi_tac.y: You have different appetites for risk: one side wants to expand, the other wants to hold steady.
doi_tac.nen: Agree in advance the most each side is willing to lose on a project, and write it into the contract.

sep.y: You and your manager work differently, so their feedback can sound like criticism.
sep.nen: Ask them to give feedback with concrete examples, and write it down so you get it right next time.

cha_me_con.y: Parent and child live at different rhythms, so a reminder easily sounds like a reproach.
cha_me_con.nen: Swap "why don't you…" for "I'd like you to try…" — short sentences, one thing at a time.

gia_dinh.y: These relatives have different temperaments, so comments on each other's private matters easily hurt.
gia_dinh.nen: Only give advice when asked; otherwise help with concrete actions.

nguoi_yeu.y: You easily agree on where to go out, how to spend money or long-term plans.
nguoi_yeu.nen: Make the most of being in sync to plan the next six months together.

vo_chong.y: As a couple you reach joint decisions quickly and rarely need to bring in a third person.
vo_chong.nen: Write down the big decisions you have made so you do not remember them differently later.

ban_be.y: You easily get each other to try new things, because your ways of thinking fit.
ban_be.nen: Learn a skill or run a small project together — this fit is likely to produce results.

dong_nghiep.y: In meetings you tend to back each other's ideas and easily become the core of the team.
dong_nghiep.nen: Make a point of inviting others' input, so the team does not feel the two of you decide alone.

doi_tac.y: You easily agree on strategy, and contract talks have few snags.
doi_tac.nen: Still settle everything with complete paperwork, because easy agreement is when details get skipped.

sep.y: Your manager listens to your ideas easily, and your proposals have a good chance of approval.
sep.nen: Bring numbers and a fallback plan with each proposal so they can approve it faster.

cha_me_con.y: Parent and child easily agree when choosing a school, a career or a big family matter.
cha_me_con.nen: Let the younger one speak first and the older one after — it keeps the child's confidence.

gia_dinh.y: At home, the two of you easily agree when a shared family decision has to be made.
gia_dinh.nen: Take the role of opening the discussion when relatives need to settle something, so others can follow easily.

nguoi_yeu.y: Each of you has your own way of thinking, but you do not tread on each other's toes.
nguoi_yeu.nen: Agree which matters one person decides and which ones you decide together.

vo_chong.y: You think along two parallel tracks: small things are fine, but big things need time to discuss.
vo_chong.nen: For spending above a limit you set together, sleep on it before deciding.

ban_be.y: You rarely agree straight away, but you rarely argue about it either.
ban_be.nen: When planning an outing, each suggests two options and you pick the one you both listed.

dong_nghiep.y: You work in two different ways without getting in each other's way.
dong_nghiep.nen: Split the work into separate parts and only combine them at the final step.

doi_tac.y: You each see the market from your own angle: complementary, but slow to close decisions.
doi_tac.nen: Set a deadline for each decision; past it, go with the plan of whoever owns that area.

sep.y: Your manager and you think differently but are not at odds.
sep.nen: Ask what matters most to them in the task you are given, and stick to it.

cha_me_con.y: Parent and child think like different generations: not opposed, but rarely of one mind.
cha_me_con.nen: Ask "what do you think?" before giving your own view, even on small things.

gia_dinh.y: Everyone in the family has their own view, but nobody wants to fight over who decides.
gia_dinh.nen: Give each shared task one person in charge, and let the others give input once.

nguoi_yeu.y: When a choice has to be made, you pull in two directions and each feels sure of being right.
nguoi_yeu.nen: Try "this time your way, next time mine" and keep track so it stays fair.

vo_chong.y: As a couple you may compete over who decides about money, the home or how to raise the children.
vo_chong.nen: Give each person their own decision areas outright; shared areas need both to nod.

ban_be.y: You easily argue to the bitter end, even about things that do not matter.
ban_be.nen: Set a playful rule: if a debate runs past five minutes, change the subject.

dong_nghiep.y: You may compete over the direction of a shared project, and meetings can drag on.
dong_nghiep.nen: Ask the team lead to settle who decides which part at the very start of the project.

doi_tac.y: You easily disagree about where to grow, especially when choosing between quick profit and lasting value.
doi_tac.nen: Write into your agreement how to break a deadlock, for example by asking a mediator you both trust.

sep.y: You and your manager may disagree on how to do things, and you can feel your hands are tied.
sep.nen: Do it their way once, record the result, then propose your way with figures.

cha_me_con.y: Parent and child may clash when choosing a direction for the future.
cha_me_con.nen: Each writes down three reasons and reads them to the other, without jumping to a conclusion yet.

gia_dinh.y: These relatives easily argue over who is right when discussing family affairs or shared property.
gia_dinh.nen: When shared matters involve money, write minutes signed by everyone.

nguoi_yeu.y: Side by side, you feel at ease and your daily habits easily fit together.
nguoi_yeu.nen: Keep a few shared rituals, like breakfast together; they keep this fit lasting.

vo_chong.y: Your household routines fit easily: bedtime, mealtimes and tidying need little discussion.
vo_chong.nen: When a baby arrives or work changes, sit down early to reset the household routine before it drifts.

ban_be.y: Going out together, sharing a room or travelling together all feel comfortable.
ban_be.nen: Plan one longer trip together each year — this friendship travels well.

dong_nghiep.y: Sitting near each other at work is pleasant, with few irritations over each other's habits.
dong_nghiep.nen: Ask to sit in the same team or close by when there is an urgent project.

doi_tac.y: The two sides feel trust when meeting, and day-to-day communication flows.
doi_tac.nen: Use that trust to agree a regular reporting routine; do not rely on feelings alone.

sep.y: Your manager feels at ease working with you, and the team atmosphere is lighter.
sep.nen: Take on the tasks that need close coordination with them; that is where you shine.

cha_me_con.y: Parent and child have matching routines, with few petty clashes under one roof.
cha_me_con.nen: Protect the times when the whole family is together, like dinner; they grow more precious with the years.

gia_dinh.y: These relatives get along, family gatherings are fun and awkward moments are rare.
gia_dinh.nen: Be the ones who gather the whole family for the holidays; the two of you make a good bridge.

nguoi_yeu.y: Your zodiac animals lean neither towards a match nor a snag — comfort depends on how you treat each other every day.
nguoi_yeu.nen: Notice the small habits the other dislikes and cut them back one at a time.

vo_chong.y: Nothing in your household routines gets in the way, but nothing fits by itself either.
vo_chong.nen: Discuss once, clearly, your hours, chores and guests, so nobody has to guess.

ban_be.y: Your friendship is ordinary; how close you get depends on shared interests.
ban_be.nen: Find a shared interest, like a sport or a favourite dish, as a reason to meet.

dong_nghiep.y: Working together has no particular snags and no special chemistry.
dong_nghiep.nen: A lunch together helps you understand each other's work habits faster.

doi_tac.y: Communication between the two sides is ordinary and needs time to warm up.
doi_tac.nen: Schedule regular face-to-face meetings in addition to online calls.

sep.y: The relationship with your manager is ordinary: neither hard nor easy.
sep.nen: Ask whether they prefer updates by message or in person.

cha_me_con.y: Parent and child fit at an ordinary level; small clashes come and go.
cha_me_con.nen: Give everyone a corner of the home to retreat to when they want quiet.

gia_dinh.y: These two relatives are not very close, but there is nothing awkward between them either.
gia_dinh.nen: Checking in on birthdays and holidays is enough to keep it warm.

nguoi_yeu.y: You can rub each other the wrong way over small things: being late, leaving things around, replying slowly.
nguoi_yeu.nen: Gather the small things and raise them once a week, rather than commenting all day long.

vo_chong.y: Your household routines can drift apart: one likes quiet, the other company; one sleeps early, the other stays up.
vo_chong.nen: Agree quiet hours at home and which days guests are welcome.

ban_be.y: On long outings you may grow tired of each other's habits.
ban_be.nen: Meet in reasonable doses, and on longer trips keep some time for yourselves.

dong_nghiep.y: Sitting close for long can grate: noise, ways of talking, working hours.
dong_nghiep.nen: Agree how to contact each other during work, for example messaging before coming over to the desk.

doi_tac.y: The two sides can misunderstand each other day to day; one remark may be heard differently.
doi_tac.nen: Confirm everything by email or recorded messages; do not settle things on a spoken word alone.

sep.y: Your daily working style and your manager's can get on each other's nerves.
sep.nen: Ask in advance when and in what format they want reports, then keep to it.

cha_me_con.y: Living together, parent and child may squabble over hours, food and phones.
cha_me_con.nen: Set few rules but keep them consistently, with parents following them as well as children.

gia_dinh.y: At family gatherings, these two may trade sharp words.
gia_dinh.nen: Sit next to people you get on with and avoid divisive topics at the table.

nguoi_yeu.y: You easily like the same kind of home, the same favourite coffee shops and the same seats.
nguoi_yeu.nen: When you think about moving in together, a home direction that suits you both is usually easy to find.

vo_chong.y: As a couple you agree about where to live, so buying a home and arranging it causes few snags.
vo_chong.nen: Look up the directions that suit your birth years to choose desk and bed directions for both of you.

ban_be.y: Sharing a room or a workplace feels comfortable for you both.
ban_be.nen: If you are thinking of renting together, you are an easy pair to live with.

dong_nghiep.y: Sitting in the same work area helps you both focus.
dong_nghiep.nen: Ask to sit near each other when the team rearranges desks.

doi_tac.y: The two sides easily agree on where to put an office or shop.
doi_tac.nen: When choosing premises, both go and view before signing.

sep.y: You and your manager feel comfortable working in the same room.
sep.nen: Take on in-person working sessions with them rather than only online.

cha_me_con.y: Parent and child fit well under one roof, rarely fighting over rooms or corners.
cha_me_con.nen: Let your child arrange their study corner their own way; parents only suggest which way to face.

gia_dinh.y: These relatives get along living nearby or together, with few disagreements about the house.
gia_dinh.nen: When renovating a shared house, these two should plan the layout together.

nguoi_yeu.y: You share the same taste in homes — easy to choose, but you may both overlook what is convenient for others.
nguoi_yeu.nen: When choosing a home, ask an outsider to have a look so nothing is missed.

vo_chong.y: As a couple you belong to the same direction group, so choosing a home is easy to agree on.
vo_chong.nen: One person's table of good directions is enough for both of you.

ban_be.y: You like the same kind of places, so outings or living together need little discussion.
ban_be.nen: Now and then try a new meeting spot so it does not get stale.

dong_nghiep.y: You both like the same kind of seat, so you are easy to place side by side.
dong_nghiep.nen: Agree clearly on shared desks and supplies so nothing gets mixed up.

doi_tac.y: The two sides have the same taste in business locations and choose quickly.
doi_tac.nen: Still view at least two places before deciding; easy agreement can lead to a rushed choice.

sep.y: Your manager and you have the same taste in workspace.
sep.nen: Offer ideas on the layout when the team moves office; your view is likely to be heard.

cha_me_con.y: Parent and child choose places in a similar way, so living together is easy.
cha_me_con.nen: Keep a private corner for your child even in a small home, so they have a place of their own.

gia_dinh.y: These relatives like the same kind of home and rarely argue about housing.
gia_dinh.nen: Take turns hosting gatherings at each other's homes; everyone will feel at ease.

nguoi_yeu.y: You have different tastes in homes: one likes bright, the other private; one likes the city, the other quiet.
nguoi_yeu.nen: If you move in together, each keeps a corner arranged their own way, and shared rooms get a middle-ground style.

vo_chong.y: As a couple you may disagree when buying a home, choosing a direction or arranging furniture.
vo_chong.nen: Favour the direction that suits whoever holds the title, and set up each private study to suit the person who uses it.

ban_be.y: Living together for long, you may get annoyed by how the other arranges things.
ban_be.nen: Travelling together is fine; if you rent together, give each person their own room.

dong_nghiep.y: Sitting right next to each other can feel cramped and make it hard to focus.
dong_nghiep.nen: If possible, sit one desk apart or face different directions.

doi_tac.y: The two sides find it hard to agree on where to put an office or shop.
doi_tac.nen: Let whoever runs day-to-day operations choose the place, and let the other give input once.

sep.y: Working in the same room as your manager may feel confining.
sep.nen: Ask for a workspace of your own or some remote days if the company allows it.

cha_me_con.y: Parent and child may disagree about rooms and when shared spaces are used.
cha_me_con.nen: Give each person a room or a corner, and knock before going in.

gia_dinh.y: Relatives living together may clash over the layout of the house and who uses which room.
gia_dinh.nen: Separate clearly what is shared and what is private, and write it down so nobody has to keep reminding.

nguoi_yeu.y: The other person's birth year lands on your love life, your sense of self and your inner life in a favourable way: with them, you feel lighter.
nguoi_yeu.nen: Tell them what you value about them, naming one specific thing they did this week.

vo_chong.y: The chart shows the other person bringing ease into your marriage, your household and your peace of mind.
vo_chong.nen: Set one shared family goal for this year together, such as a savings target or a trip.

ban_be.y: The other person touches your friendships and siblings in a good way: often the one who introduces and supports you.
ban_be.nen: When you need to widen your circle, this friend is the first one to ask.

dong_nghiep.y: The other person brings ease into your work and your relationships at the workplace.
dong_nghiep.nen: Suggest working together on important projects; the two of you get things done.

doi_tac.y: The chart shows the other person touching your money and work in a helpful way.
doi_tac.nen: Start with one small deal, and expand step by step once it shows results.

sep.y: This manager brings ease into your work: likely to open doors and hand you good assignments.
sep.nen: Ask them for one piece of career advice each quarter; they can point you in the right direction.

cha_me_con.y: The chart shows the two of you supporting each other in family life and in spirit.
cha_me_con.nen: Write down a few pieces of advice or happy memories of each other, to read again when times are hard.

gia_dinh.y: This relative brings ease into your ties with siblings, parents and home.
gia_dinh.nen: When the family has something big on, this is the person to take charge of it with you.

nguoi_yeu.y: The other person's birth year touches your chart lightly, leaning neither towards ease nor snags in love.
nguoi_yeu.nen: Keep one evening a week just for the two of you — this relationship grows from things you do together.

vo_chong.y: Your two charts touch at a moderate level; the marriage is shaped by how you nurture it.
vo_chong.nen: Once a month, ask each other "what would we like to change this month?" and pick one thing to do.

ban_be.y: This friend touches your chart lightly; how close you are is up to the two of you.
ban_be.nen: Message to check in when you do not need anything; that is how friendships last.

dong_nghiep.y: Your charts touch at a moderate level at work; how well you coordinate depends on how you divide tasks.
dong_nghiep.nen: After each shared project, take fifteen minutes to name what went well and what to change.

doi_tac.y: The chart shows no clear ease or snag around money and business with this person.
doi_tac.nen: Judge by real results after the first three months before putting in more capital.

sep.y: This manager touches your work at a moderate level.
sep.nen: Keep regular one-to-one meetings with them so the relationship grows through real work.

cha_me_con.y: The parent's and child's charts touch lightly; closeness depends on the time you give each other.
cha_me_con.nen: Once a week, a call or a meal just to chat, with no instructions.

gia_dinh.y: This relative touches your chart at an ordinary level.
gia_dinh.nen: Stay in touch regularly at family occasions; no more is needed.

nguoi_yeu.y: The other person's birth year lands where you care most in love: easy to expect a lot, easy to feel hurt.
nguoi_yeu.nen: Say plainly one thing you hope for at a time; do not wait for them to work it out.

vo_chong.y: The chart shows marriage as the area you both take most to heart: a small remark can easily become a big deal.
vo_chong.nen: When angry, agree to talk again after an hour, never while tempers are hot.

ban_be.y: This friend touches the part of you that worries about friends: borrowing and favours can get tangled.
ban_be.nen: Keep money clear with this friend; if you lend, lend only what you are prepared not to get back.

dong_nghiep.y: The chart shows shared work as where you misunderstand each other, especially about credit.
dong_nghiep.nen: Name who did each part in shared reports.

doi_tac.y: The other person's birth year lands on your money and work in a way that calls for care.
doi_tac.nen: Keep a separate joint account, and require two signatures for large payments.

sep.y: This manager touches your work in a pressured way: high demands, easy to feel displeased.
sep.nen: Confirm the request by message after each assignment.

cha_me_con.y: The chart shows parent and child worrying about each other too much, so love turns heavy.
cha_me_con.nen: Each names one thing they want to handle themselves; the other only asks how it is going and does not take over.

gia_dinh.y: This relative touches your home and sibling ties in a way where shared matters easily get tangled.
gia_dinh.nen: Put shared property and money matters within the family clearly in writing.

chua_tinh_cung_phi: Not scored yet because one person's gender is missing — add it to get all five criteria. The total has been rescaled over the remaining four.

de_hoa_hop.mo_ta: Most criteria lean towards a good fit. The two of you understand each other without much effort.

hop_neu_hieu.mo_ta: Some areas fit, some differ. Knowing the differences in advance makes it easier to give way at the right moment.

can_dung_hoa_nhieu.nhan: Needs a lot of give and take
can_dung_hoa_nhieu.mo_ta: Many criteria differ. The two of you need to say what you want and divide tasks more clearly than most pairs.

nhieu_khac_biet.mo_ta: You differ in many ways. Different does not mean incompatible — it just means talking more clearly, and sooner.

nguoi_yeu: Say one specific thank-you every day.
When upset, say "I need ten minutes", then come back and keep talking.
vo_chong: A fifteen-minute family meeting each week: money, children, chores.
Give each person their own decision areas.
Keep one date night just for the two of you each month.
ban_be: Meet regularly, even when there is nothing special to talk about.
Keep money clear when you go out together.
dong_nghiep: Settle who does which part at the hand-over meeting.
Give clear credit in joint reports.
Give feedback in private and praise in front of the team.
doi_tac: Hold a monthly meeting to reconcile the figures.
Write down in advance how to handle disagreements.
sep: Confirm requests by message after taking on a task.
Ask for feedback regularly, note it down and act on it.
cha_me_con: One shared meal a week with no talk of school or money.
Parents say "we trust you" more often than giving instructions.
gia_dinh: When shared matters involve money, put it on paper.
Meet at holidays and keep the topics light.
Help each other with concrete actions rather than advice.

loi_dan: This score is a reference, based on folk rules and the Zi Wei Dou Shu and Eight Mansions books. Whether a relationship goes well depends on how the two of you treat each other every day.

tieu_de.phu_the_trung_menh_nguoi_kia: The other person is close to the partner your chart describes
tieu_de.hai_nguoi_sat_pha_tham: Both of you like to make your own calls
tieu_de.dong_tinh_bu_nhau: One opens new paths, the other keeps things steady

cach_doc_them.dan_kia: Read from the other person's side — here "you" means the other person:
cach_doc_them.can_cu_chung: A reading from a modern three-harmonies school of Zi Wei Dou Shu, rewritten by our editors in plain language. This part is not counted in the score.
